The core of the court's reasoning rests on what is now being called the browser analogy: an AI agent is no more Perplexity accessing Amazon than Safari is Apple accessing Amazon. By this logic, the court held that the AI assistant is "a tool, not a person for statutory purposes," and that the user, not the agent maker, is responsible for the actions taken. The ruling is narrow but precedent-setting. [...]
